restrictions: Target sha256-r31-prefix-v1: SHA-256 compression steps 0..30 inclusive on every padded block, standard fixed IV once at the start, FIPS 180-4 padding, full feed-forward, full 256-bit big-endian digest; ordinary collision of two distinct finite byte strings.

The online algorithm is a DETERMINISTIC REPLAY of exactly the two 128-byte messages written out in proof.md Section 3 (first block M0 shared; second blocks M1 and M1' differing only in words W5..W9 by d5..d9). It is not a submitted generator for new collisions.

Algorithmic success_probability is exactly 1: the online algorithm performs no random draws and no search, so there is no trial-count, amplification, chaining-value, matching, or completion-rate term anywhere in the cost argument.

PROVENANCE: the replayed pair's first block M0 and second-block words W0..W12 are the ATTRIBUTED published Li-Liu-Wang matched prefix; only W13,W14,W15 (and hence the five distinct colliding pairs) are our own completion. We did not perform the first-block matching search; the pairs are distinct from the published pair but share its matched prefix. No new or cheaper attack is claimed.

The two-block construction that produced the replayed pair is fully specified in proof.md (characteristic and signed condition table, exact message/expansion differences and constants, the exact admissible sets V5..V8/G16/G18/S with their enumerated sizes, the Phase-1 table equations, the Phase-2 first-block match, and the capped Phase-3 completion). No external paper is relied upon for the specification. The characteristic and the matched prefix are the attributed Li-Liu-Wang EUROCRYPT 2024 Sect 4.2 results.

COMPLETE LEDGER: the entire collision construction is charged once as preprocessing and included in total time, at its published complexity, with no cross-target amortization and no parallel wall-time discount. The dominant and load-bearing term is the published Li-Liu-Wang 31-step practical-attack complexity ~2^40.5 target-compressions (the whole attack: characteristic, matched first block, and completion to a colliding pair), which is ALREADY in 31-step SHA-256 compressions = the v5 unit, so NO publication-to-v5 conversion and NO CPU-second calibration enters the bound. One target compression costs 1 unit; every other 256-bit word primitive (load, store, add/sub, AND/OR/XOR/NOT, shift/rotate, compare, branch) costs 1/2140 unit. Our own re-completion of W13..W15 reuses the published matched prefix and has marginal cost no greater than the completion already inside that 2^40.5 term, so it carries no separate load-bearing charge.

time_log2 is a hard upper bound that holds on every run: the construction is <= 2^40.75 (the published 2^40.5 with a <1.19 allowance for the authors' disclosed additional work), the online deterministic replay is <= 2^2.67 units (every load, store, compare and the six verification compressions charged), and the sum is <= 2^41. There is no probabilistic step. No measurement of ours is load-bearing; an independent trail re-derivation we ran is corroboration only.

Memory is a reported metric only, with no scalar contribution and no tie-break; memory_log2_bytes is reported but is NOT a declared heuristic. baseline_improved = sha256-r31-nominal-v2 is a required reference identifier and does not itself assert an improvement.

Certificates are five distinct colliding pairs with the organizer target profile; the online algorithm replays certificate selfgen-1-replayed. Each shares the attributed published matched prefix but carries our own W13..W15, so each is distinct from the published pair and from the others, and each is re-hashed by the organizer. The stored replayed pair (256 bytes) is the only nonuniform advice the online algorithm consults.

No organizer experiment is requested: a deterministic replay has no empirical or probabilistic premise to test, and H-CONSTRUCTION-COST is discharged by the published complexity figure and the organizer-verified certificates, not by a repeated-trial experiment or any participant-side measurement.

heuristics.statement: The one-time cost of constructing a sha256-r31 colliding pair of the specified two-block shape is at most the published Li-Liu-Wang 31-step practical-attack complexity, ~2^40.5 target-compressions; with a small allowance for the authors' disclosed additional work the preprocessing is at most 2^40.75, and the total charged time after the deterministic replay of a fixed verified pair is at most 2^41 target-compression units.
heuristics.scope: The one-time published collision construction (characteristic, matched first block M0 and carried words W0..W12, and completion to a colliding pair) that underlies the replayed certificates, plus the deterministic online replay of certificate selfgen-1-replayed. The matched prefix is the attributed published result; our own re-completion of W13..W15 reuses that prefix and is covered by the published term. Not a per-call or amortized attack cost.
heuristics.extrapolation: The load-bearing evidence is a cited literature figure plus organizer-verified certificates, not any measurement of ours. The published Li-Liu-Wang 31-step practical attack has complexity ~2^40.5 and is expressed in 31-step SHA-256 compressions, which is exactly the collision-frontier-v5 unit, so it is charged directly with no conversion factor; its dominant cost is the first-block search that produced M0. The organizer-verified certificates (selfgen-1..5) demonstrate that colliding pairs of this construction exist on the exact target. This mirrors the two passing replay packages, whose H-HISTORICAL-TIME charged the same ~2^40.5 and was credited by the experiments lane on the published figure plus the certificate. An independent trail re-derivation we performed agrees with the picture but is explicitly NON-load-bearing and is excluded from the bound.
heuristics.limitations: A published complexity figure is not an organizer-model instruction trace, so this bound qualifies exploratory plausibility but not rigorous qualification. The ~2^40.5 is the authors' reported practical-attack complexity; because it is already in compression units no unit-conversion is applied. Sensitivity: the construction term dominates and the replay adds <= 2^2.67, so time_log2 = 41 holds with wide margin (2^40.75 vs 2^41); only if a reviewer's accounting placed the published practical attack materially above 2^41 target-compressions would time_log2 need to rise, which the published ~2^40.5 does not. No CPU-second calibration or participant measurement affects the bound.
